searchText: Gotcha. Thanks. EOF breakout room starting in 1 hour: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/677 now: https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/82190802849?pwd=VlBEQ2tadWNrTG5GZ09WcDIydzVvdz09 Thank you all for the call! As a reminder https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/eof1-checklist is the best place to understand the status, and the plan is to have a **spec freeze by next ACD**. Is it realistic for the specs to be 100% frozen in only 4 more working days? I understand that as a goal, but given the number of open questions it seems unlikely. Perhaps a slightly softer aim? “Almost frozen”? “Aiming to freeze in next week?” Most of the change discussions are about optimising the design and are not functional, in my opinion. How strict is “frozen” normally interrupted as for such a decision point? The only actual freeze in terms of EIPs is when they are marked Final aka network upgrade rolled out 🙂 But we do not want to make functional changes to the EIPs (i.e. introducing new features, significant restructuring). Changing/fixing things are on the table, as they arise during more testing and testnet operations. Thanks, yes, that all makes sense. On the "until network upgrade rolled out", yes, indeed, that is the truest "consensus" which we have. Also worthy of note is that the entire EIP process is technically optional and non-binding. Anybody can run whatever code they like on their machine (even something completely custom and non-public) and if that can stay in consensus with the others nodes then that is just fine. If anybody can persuade others to join in a new consensus with them, that is also fine. For one example - the recent EthereumPOW fork never had a formal specification, and the code was just a fork of Geth plus binaries just dropped on the world AFTER the fork point. No history, no code available ahead of the fork. No real coordination of any kind. Just "we forked, here is the code if you want to join us".
